No one will snatch Christ’s sheep out of His hand (10:28). The warning is aimed at the man who stands near the Vine for years and never draws life from it. Nearness is not union. The cure for dry wood is to come to Christ, today, as you are.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: MY WORDS, MY LOVE, MY JOY
pulls: The Father’s love for the Son has no floor and no end. Jesus says that is the measure of His love for you. You are not told to make that love. You are told to stay in it.
paras: If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you. This is no blank check, and it is not a lever for getting your way. A man whose mind is soaked in Christ’s words starts to want what Christ wants. His asking changes. He asks for fruit, and the Father, who loves fruit, gives it.

In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples. The fruit is not there to build your name. It brings glory to the Father, and it marks you as belonging to Christ. Fruit is what His life looks like from outside — love that holds when it is not returned, patience through a long winter, a clean word where a cutting one used to come out, a hand opened where it used to close.

Then Jesus tells you where the life in the branch comes from. Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love. Measure that if you can. The Father’s love for the Son has no floor and no end, and that is the measure of Christ’s love for you. You are not told to make that love. You are told to stay in it.

He shows you how He Himself remained: He kept His Father’s commandments. Keeping does not get a son into the house; it is how he lives once he is home. And He tells you why He has said all this: that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full. Christ wants His own joy running in you, full to the brim.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: CHOSEN AND APPOINTED
paras: This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you. Again the measure comes first. Christ loved, and then He commands love. Then He shows what His love looks like: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends. Within a day He will do exactly that, on a cross near the city, for men who will scatter that same night.

You are my friends, if you do whatever I command you. Do not hear that backwards. Jesus is not hiring friends who meet His terms. He is describing men He has already made His friends, and the next line tells you how He did it. No longer do I call you servants, He says, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. A servant gets orders. A friend gets told what the master is doing, and Christ has made known to you everything He heard from His Father.

Then comes the line that ends every boast. You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain. You did not pick Him out of a lineup. He picked you before you knew His name, and He set you in place on purpose. The fruit was His idea before it was ever yours.

Fruit that remains — not a burst of effort that fades by spring, but a life God keeps. And the passage ends where the love began: I command these things to you, that you may love one another. The love you need for your wife, your brother, the man at church you cannot stand, does not start with you. It flows from the Vine who chose you and died for you.

stations.verse: I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.
stations.question: Before He said a word about the branches, Jesus said, I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer; what in my life with God have I been trying to grow out of my own root instead of His?
stations.gloss: a vine, the grapevine
body: Ampelos is the word for a vine. It appears in only nine verses of the New Testament. Three belong to the Lord’s Supper, where Jesus says He will not drink of this fruit of the vine again until He drinks it new in His Father’s Kingdom (Matthew 26:29). Three are here.

I am the true vine. Not one vine among many, and not a copy — the one Israel was planted to be and never was. Joined to Him, a man has life. Cut off from Him, he has wood. Jesus says this to men who have walked with Him three years, so they will know the life never came from them.

The dust says you are your own root, that if anything good is going to grow in your life you will have to raise it out of your own soil. Ampelos answers with a Person. Christ is the vine, and the life is in Him. Your place is to be a branch, and that place was given.
stations.live: Each morning this week, before you leave the house, say it plainly: ‘Christ is the vine. My Father is the farmer. I am a branch, and I live from Him today.’

stations.verse: Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.
stations.question: The Father prunes the branch that bears fruit, that it may bear more fruit; what cutting back in my life this year have I read as His absence when it is His care?
stations.gloss: to bear, carry; to bring forth fruit
body: Pherō means to bear or carry, to endure, to bring something forward, and of plants, to bear fruit. It stands in sixty verses. Hebrews uses it of the Son upholding all things by the word of his power (1:3). John uses it of the grain of wheat that falls into the ground, dies, and bears much fruit (12:24).

In this chapter the word keeps coming back: bear fruit, bear more fruit, bear much fruit. Notice what the branch does. It carries what the vine sends through it. It does not make the grapes; it holds them up to the sun. The fruit in your life — love that lasts, patience with a slow son, honesty about money — is Christ’s life carried by you.

The dust wants you to hear the pruning as a threat to the man who is trying. It is the opposite. The Father prunes because there is fruit. The Son who carries all things carries you, and every cut the Father makes serves the harvest to come.
stations.live: Name one cut the Father has made in your life this year. Instead of asking why, ask this: ‘Father, what fruit are You making room for?’ Write down whatever comes to mind.

stations.verse: If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
stations.question: Jesus warned that the man who does not remain in Him is thrown out as a branch and is withered; where has my faith dried into habit and church talk with no living hold on Christ Himself?
stations.gloss: to dry up, wither
body: Xērainō is built on the word for dry. It means to dry up, to parch, to wither. Fifteen verses carry it, most of them about plants: the seed on rocky ground that had no root and withered away (Mark 4:6), the fig tree with leaves and no fruit, the grass that withers under the sun.

That is the branch of 15:6. It did not dry out because the vine ran short of sap. It dried out because it never drew from the vine. A man can stand close to Christ for years — singing the songs, knowing the words, sitting in the same pew — and have no root in Him at all.

The dust tells you a dry season proves God has given up on you. But the warning is a mercy, given while there is still time. A dry man does not need a better plan. He needs the Vine. Come to Christ as you are; He will in no way throw out the man who comes (6:37).
stations.live: Name the place where your faith has gone dry and runs on habit. Take that place to Christ in prayer this week: ‘Lord, I am dry here. You said You will not throw out the man who comes.’

stations.verse: If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
stations.question: Jesus spoke plainly of fruitless branches thrown into the fire, and they are burned; what am I quietly trusting to keep me safe on the last day that is not Christ Himself?
stations.gloss: to kindle, light; to burn
body: Kaiō means to light or kindle, as a lamp is lit, and then to burn, even to burn up. Thirteen verses use it. Jesus called John the Baptist the burning and shining lamp (5:35). The two men on the Emmaus road asked, Weren’t our hearts burning within us, while the risen Lord opened the Scriptures to them (Luke 24:32).

Here it is fire of another kind. Dry branches are gathered and burned. Jesus does not soften it. Judgment is real, and the man who never drew life from Christ will not escape it by having stood near Him. Jesus says this on the night before He goes to the cross to bear judgment for every branch that is truly His.

The dust either laughs at the fire or uses it to scare you into effort. Christ does neither. He warns you so you will run to Him while the door stands open. The same word that burns dead wood sets a heart burning when He opens the Scriptures.
stations.live: Read John 15:1–8 aloud this week with your wife or a friend. Do not argue about the fire. Ask each other one thing: ‘What am I trusting that is not Christ?’ Then pray over the answer.

stations.verse: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
stations.question: Jesus named the greatest love as laying down his life for his friends, then called the eleven His friends and went to the cross; where am I still living like a servant earning His favor instead of a friend He died for?
stations.gloss: to place, set; to lay down
body: Tithēmi is a working word: to place, lay, set, put down. It shows up in 96 verses — a lamp set on a stand, the dead laid in a tomb, Jesus laying aside His outer garments to wash feet (13:4). It is also the word for laying down a life, used of the good shepherd in chapter 10 and in Peter’s promise of 13:37.

Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends. Jesus does not just describe that love. He does it the next day, of His own will. Three verses on, the same verb stands behind appointed you. The One who laid down His life for you also set you in place for fruit.

The dust tells you love is a feeling you either have or you don’t. Tithēmi says love is a life laid down. You cannot lay yours down for your wife until you have seen His laid down for you. Look there first.
stations.live: Pick one thing to lay down this week for someone in your house — an evening, your right to be right, a purchase you wanted. Do it without announcing it, and tell Christ: ‘You laid Yours down first.’

practices.title: LET HIS WORDS REMAIN
practices.body: Jesus ties remaining in Him to His words remaining in you. Pick one verse from 15:1–17 each day and carry it — on a card in your wallet, taped to the dash, stuck above the kitchen sink. Read it before work and again at lunch. Say it aloud on the drive home and once more before you sleep. You are not filling a quota. You are staying close to the Vine through the very words He left you.

practices.title: NAME THE PRUNING
practices.body: Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes. Sit down one evening and write out what has been cut back in your life this year — the job, the plan, the health, the friend. Beside each one, write what has grown in its place, if anything has yet. Then hand the list to the Father in prayer and ask Him what fruit He is making room for. The shears are in a Father’s hand, and He does not waste a cut.

practices.title: QUIT PRODUCING ON YOUR OWN STEAM
practices.body: Apart from me you can do nothing. Pick the one place where you have been grinding at holiness by willpower alone — the temper, the screen after dark, the tongue at home. Stop treating it as a project you will finish. Each time it rises this week, say to Christ: ‘I cannot bear this fruit. You can bear it through me.’ Then do the next right thing, leaning your weight on Him and not on your resolve.

practices.title: LAY SOMETHING DOWN
practices.body: Christ commands you to love one another, even as I have loved you, and His love laid down a life. Choose one person this week — your wife, a son, a brother at church who grates on you — and lay down something real for them. Your Saturday morning. Your right to the last word. The money you had set aside for yourself. Do it quietly, without keeping score, because He did it first for you.

practices.title: ASK FOR FRUIT THAT REMAINS
practices.body: Jesus chose and appointed you that your fruit should remain, and in the same breath He tied that to asking the Father in His name. Each night this week, before you sleep, ask the Father for one specific fruit in one specific place — patience with your daughter, honesty in Thursday’s deal, kindness to the man who works beside you. Ask in Jesus’ name. Then watch for the answer, and thank Him when it comes.

title: The True Vine
subtitle: from dust to fruit that remains
keyVerse: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

passage.text: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.
Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.
You are already pruned clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.
Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned.
If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you.
“In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.
Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and remain in his love.
I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.
“This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you.
Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends, if you do whatever I command you.
No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you.

You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.
“I command these things to you, that you may love one another.

stationsIntro: Take each verse the way a farmer walks a row — slowly, looking close at what is growing. Answer the question in plain words, then let the Greek word point you back to the Vine who holds the branch.
lifeIntro: Jesus put it plainly: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you. The Vine holds the branch, and the Father tends it with His own hands. Here are five ways a branch stays close to the life that feeds it this week.
lifePulls: Christ chose you, made you clean by His word, and laid down His life for you before He said one word about your fruit. Everything He asks this week grows out of that. Nothing He asks replaces it.
prayer: Father, You are the farmer, and Your Son is the true vine. Thank You that You chose me before I chose You, and that I am already clean because of the word Jesus has spoken. Thank You that He laid down His life for me and calls me His friend. Keep me in Him, and keep His words in me. Where You prune, give me eyes to see Your care and not Your absence. Forgive me for straining to bear fruit without Him, and for the dry places I have called faith. Let His love hold me, His joy fill me, and His fruit grow in me and remain. Teach me to love the people in my house as Christ has loved me. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, You are the farmer, and Your Son is the true vine.
Thank You that You chose me before I chose You, and that I am already clean
because of the word Jesus has spoken.
Thank You that He laid down His life for me and calls me His friend.
Keep me in Him, and keep His words in me.
Where You prune, give me eyes to see Your care and not Your absence.
Forgive me for straining to bear fruit without Him, and for the dry places I have
called faith.
Let His love hold me, His joy fill me, and His fruit grow in me and remain.
Teach me to love the people in my house as Christ has loved me.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: Christ is the true vine, and His Father is the farmer. You are a branch — made clean by His word, pruned by the Father’s hand, alive only as you remain in Him. Apart from Him you can do nothing, and the branch that never drew from Him withers and burns. He chose you, laid down His life for you, and appointed you to bear fruit that remains. Stay close. The fruit is His.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, and find the Vine that was planted for you. Look to the Son who said, I am the true vine, and meant that every bit of life you will ever bear must come up out of Him. Look to the Father who tends the branches with His own hands and never cuts without a purpose. Look to the Friend who told you everything He heard from His Father and kept nothing back.

The dust has kept you producing. It handed you the quota and the deadline and told you a man is what he brings in. You have worked your faith like a second shift, and some weeks the rows look fine from the road. But hear the Vine. Apart from me you can do nothing. That sentence was never meant to shame you. It is the gate out of the second shift. You were never meant to be the root, and you were never asked to be.

Look at what He did with His own life. Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends. He said it at night and did it the next day, on a cross near the city. He went there and bore the judgment that dry wood deserves, so that no branch truly joined to Him will ever be thrown into the fire. Then the grave gave Him back, and the Vine lives, and every branch in Him lives from His life.

So take this into Tuesday. You did not choose Him. He chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit — fruit that remains. The Father’s knife on your life this year is a farmer’s care, not a judge’s sentence. You are already clean because of the word He has spoken to you, and nothing the dust says can make you unclean again. Stay close to that word, stay in His love, and the fruit will come in its season: His life, carried in your hands, to the glory of your Father.
closingVerse: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
carry: Since Christ has told you He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, where are you straining this week to make fruit that only comes from staying in Him?

sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: The dust tells a believing man that he has been left on his own. Jesus went back to heaven a long time ago. What remains is a book on the shelf, a pew on Sunday, and whatever grit you can find before the alarm goes off. And the world, which used to leave you alone, now looks at you sideways. The men at the feed store laugh a half beat late when you don’t laugh at the joke. Your brother-in-law has a word for men like you, and he saves it for Thanksgiving.

So the dust draws its conclusions. If Jesus were really near, it would not be this hard. If you were doing it right, people would like you more. Keep your head down. Keep your faith inside the house, where it cannot cost you anything. And when you need to know what God wants, go with your gut and call it the Spirit, since no one is going to tell you plainly anyway.
A man who listens to that long enough ends up face down in it, and his prayer is the one the psalm already wrote for him: My soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV)

The reviving word here was spoken on the night before the cross, and it answers every one of those lies. The world’s hatred is the same hatred that met Jesus first. His going away was not your loss. It is to your advantage that I go away, He says, because the One He sends is the Spirit of truth. He has not left you alone with a book. He speaks through it.

sections.heading: Friends Inside, the World Outside
pulls: The dust says the world’s cold shoulder means you have failed. Jesus says the world hated Him before it hated you, and that you feel it at all because He chose you out of it.
paras: These words come late on the night Jesus was betrayed. He has washed feet, sent Judas out into the dark, and told His men about the Father’s house and the Counselor. At the end of chapter 14 He says, Arise, let’s go from here, and He keeps talking. Just before this passage He called them branches in the true Vine and friends He had chosen. Now, with no break, He turns from the love among His friends to the hatred of the world outside.

The passage runs in a straight line. The world hates Him, so it will hate them (15:18–25). The Spirit and the apostles will testify anyway (15:26–27). The hatred will come dressed as religion, and He tells them ahead of time so it will not knock them flat (16:1–4). Then He tells them why His leaving is good: the Counselor will convict the world and guide them into all truth (16:5–15). Read 15:18 through 16:15 in one sitting. Listen for how often Jesus says I have told you, or close to it. A man who has been told ahead of time is not caught off guard.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: HATED BEFORE YOU
paras: If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you. Jesus does not soften the word, and He puts Himself in front of it. Whatever the world aims at you, it aimed at Him first, and harder. Before another day was out it would drive nails through His hands. You are walking ground He has already walked, and He walked it bleeding.

Then He tells them why. If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you. The choosing comes first. You did not walk out of the world on your own legs and earn its anger as a badge. He chose you out of it, just as He said a few verses back: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you. The world’s hatred is the backwash of His choosing. It tells you whose you are.

Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ He had said it hours earlier, with the towel still damp. Then it meant that if your Lord stooped, you can stoop. Now it means that if your Lord was hated, you will be too. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.

But they will do all these things to you for my name’s sake, because they don’t know him who sent me. There is the root of it. Not your personality, and not your politics. The name, and behind the name a Father the world does not know. When the cold shoulder comes for Christ’s sake, it is the world reacting to the One you carry.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: WITHOUT A CAUSE
paras: Then Jesus says something hard about the men who turned Him away. If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. He does not mean they were sinless before He came. He means their unbelief had been dragged into the light. He did the works which no one else did. A man who hears that word, sees those works, and still turns away has nothing left to hide behind.

Then the heaviest line: But now they have seen and also hated both me and my Father. No one hates the Son while loving the Father. They are one. Jesus calls it the fulfilling of what was written, They hated me without a cause. The words come from the Psalms, from a man hated by enemies who had no reason. In Jesus they reach their full weight. Of every man ever hated, He alone gave no cause at all.

When the Counselor has come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me. Mark how Jesus speaks of the Spirit. He comes. He is sent. He testifies. That is a Person, not a force or a feeling. The Father and the Son send Him, and He comes to make one thing known: who Jesus is.

You will also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning. The apostles saw and heard, and their witness is written down in books like this one. The Spirit still testifies through it. Here the weight comes off your shoulders. The world will not be won by your cleverness. The Spirit bears the witness, and you tell what you have been given.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: BETTER THAT HE GO
pulls: Jesus told His men the hard things before they came, so that when the door shut in their faces they would remember He had seen it first. Nothing the world does to you for His name has caught Him off guard.
paras: I have said these things to you so that you wouldn’t be caused to stumble. He names the cost before it comes. They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time comes that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God. The blow would come from religious men, sure they were pleasing God. John has already shown you a healed beggar thrown out for telling the truth about the One who opened his eyes.

Saul of Tarsus was one of those men. Years later, standing before a king, he said, I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus names the root plainly: They will do these things because they have not known the Father, nor me. Zeal is not the same as knowing God. And grace reached even that man. The persecutor became an apostle.

But I have told you these things, so that when the time comes, you may remember that I told you about them. When the door shuts in your face for His name, remember. He saw it. He said it. Nothing has slipped out of His hands.

Then comes the turn. Sorrow had filled their hearts, and Jesus said, Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I don’t go away, the Counselor won’t come to you. John told you why back at the feast: the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus wasn’t yet glorified. The cross, the empty tomb, and His return to the Father had to come first. Then the Spirit would be given, not walking beside a few men on a road, but living in every believer, in every place, for good.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: HE WILL GUIDE YOU
paras: When he has come, he will convict the world about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment. He convicts about sin, because they don’t believe in me. The root sin is not the second drink or the temper. It is unbelief toward the Son. He convicts about righteousness, because I am going to my Father — the Father’s welcome of the risen Son is God’s verdict that Jesus was in the right. And about judgment, because the prince of this world has been judged. The cross that looked like Satan’s win was his sentence. So you are not the one who must convict your son or your old friend. You tell them the truth about Christ. The Spirit does the convicting.

I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now. Christ measures the load. However when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. This promise came first to the apostles. He led them into the truth they then wrote down, and the Gospel in your hands is the fruit of it. Jesus would later pray for those also who will believe in me through their word. That is you. The Spirit does not hand out new Scripture now. He opens the Word He has already given.

He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine, and will declare it to you. Here is how you test any voice that claims to be the Spirit. Does it make much of Christ? The Spirit of truth is not your gut with a halo on it. He points to the Son, and through the Son to the Father: All things that the Father has are mine.

stations.verse: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
stations.question: Jesus told His men to remember the word that I said to you — the servant is not above his lord, and the world that hated Him will hate them; where am I reading the world’s contempt as proof God has left me?
stations.gloss: to call to mind, remember; to make mention of
body: Mnēmoneuō means to call to mind, to remember, and at times to make mention of something. Twenty-one New Testament verses use it. John uses it in three verses on this one night of teaching.

Jesus tells His men to call back a word He gave them at the basin: a servant is not greater than his lord. Remembering puts the hatred in its place. His Lord met it first, and said so. In 16:4 He gives the reason for all His warnings: so that when the time comes, you may remember.

The dust wants you to forget. It wants every cold shoulder to feel like proof that God has stepped back. Mnēmoneuō hands you a memory instead. He said it would come. He went through it ahead of you. And the Lord you remember is risen.
stations.live: When the side comment or the cold shoulder comes for Christ’s sake this week, do not answer it in kind. Call back His word under your breath: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord. He told me first.’

stations.verse: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
stations.question: Jesus said that once He had come and spoken, those who turned from Him have no excuse for their sin; where do I hold up an excuse against a plain word of Christ instead of bringing Him the sin itself?
stations.gloss: a pretense, pretext; the cover offered in place of the truth
body: Prophasis means a pretense, a pretext — the reason given in place of the real one. It is found in six New Testament verses. Mark uses it of men who for a pretense make long prayers. Paul uses it when he writes that Christ is proclaimed whether in pretense or in truth. Here it is rendered excuse.

That is what Jesus took away by coming. Once He had spoken and worked among them, the cover was gone. Every man keeps a pretext ready: the way he was raised, the pressure on the night shift, the wife who does not understand him. A pretext is a tarp thrown over the real thing.

The dust says that if your excuses are pulled away, you will be left in the cold with nothing. But the One who pulled away the excuse came to die for the sin under it. You do not need a pretext before Him. You need Him, and He has already come and spoken.
stations.live: Write down the excuse you reach for most when you fall short. Draw a line through it. Under it, name the sin plainly to God, and say: ‘No cover. Christ came for this.’

stations.verse: They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time comes that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God.
stations.question: Jesus warned that men would think killing His followers offers service to God, and He said it beforehand so that you wouldn’t be caused to stumble; what opposition to my faith has shaken me as if Christ had not foretold it?
stations.gloss: to bring to; to offer, especially a sacrifice or gift to God
body: Prospherō means to bring something to someone, and very often to offer it to God — a gift, a prayer, a sacrifice. You will find it in 45 New Testament verses, more of them in Hebrews than in any other book. John uses it once more, at the cross, where a sponge of vinegar was held to Jesus’ mouth.

So 16:2 cuts deep. Men will kill the disciples and think that he offers service to God. Jesus names why: they have not known the Father, nor me. Religion with no knowledge of the Son can do great harm and feel holy doing it.

The dust tells you that you must bring God something to make yourself right — your zeal, your record. Hebrews answers with the one offering that settled it: Christ, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God. Nothing is left for you to bring but faith.
stations.live: Think of the churchgoer whose hostility has rattled you most. Pray for him by name each morning this week, and say: ‘Christ’s one offering is enough for him and for me.’

stations.verse: I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now.
stations.question: Jesus had many things left to tell His men that they could not yet bear, and the Spirit later gave them to the apostles, who wrote them down; what part of that written word am I leaving unread?
stations.gloss: to take up; to bear, carry, as a burden; to endure
body: Bastazō means to take up with the hands, then to bear or carry a burden, and so to endure. It occurs in 27 New Testament verses. John uses it of the stones men took up against Jesus, of Judas carrying off what was put in the money box, and of Jesus Himself, who went out, bearing his cross.

Here Jesus uses it of His words. I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now. He knew how much weight eleven frightened men could carry that night, and He did not pile on more. He left the rest for the Spirit to bring after the cross and the empty tomb.

The dust wants everything at once, every reason laid out before you take a step. Christ measures the load. The One who carried His own cross does not lay on you what you cannot carry. What He holds back for now, He holds for you, not against you.
stations.live: Pick one New Testament letter you have rarely read. Read a chapter a day this week, and before each one say: ‘These are the things He still had to tell them. Now He has told me.’

stations.verse: However when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.
stations.question: Jesus says the Spirit will not speak from himself, but takes what is Christ’s and declares it; what am I calling the Spirit’s leading that I could not trace back to the words of Christ?
stations.gloss: to bring back word, report; to announce, declare
body: Anangellō first meant to bring back word, to report. Later it came to mean to announce or declare. It appears in 14 New Testament verses, and three of them stand one after another here, in 16:13, 14 and 15.

Watch what the Spirit declares. He will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He takes from what is mine, Jesus says, and makes it known. He reports. He brought the apostles into the truth they wrote, and through their word He declares Christ to you.

The dust says you need a private word from heaven before you can move. But the Spirit has already declared what is Christ’s, and it lies open in front of you. He does not speak around the Word. He speaks through it, and He always ends at the Son.
stations.live: Before you call anything ‘the Lord leading me’ this week, find where it meets the words of Christ in Scripture. If you cannot, hold it loosely. Pray: ‘Spirit of truth, show me Christ in His Word.’

practices.title: REMEMBER WHO WAS HATED FIRST
practices.body: When the cold shoulder comes this week for Christ’s sake — the joke at your expense, the invitation that stops coming — read John 15:18–20 before you react. Say out loud who was hated first. Do not nurse it like a wound or wear it like a medal. It is the backwash of His choosing you. Then do one plain kindness for the man who gave it. That is what a servant of a hated Lord does, because it is what his Lord did.

practices.title: DROP ONE EXCUSE
practices.body: Jesus came and spoke, and the cover came off. Pick the excuse you use most — tired, provoked, it’s just how I am — and retire it for seven days. When you fall short, name the thing without the pretext, first to God and then, if someone was hurt, to that person. You will find that the excuse was heavier to carry than the confession. Christ died for the sin. He never asked you to defend it.

practices.title: LET THE SPIRIT CONVICT
practices.body: Think of one man you love who does not believe — a son, a brother, a man on your crew. You may have tried to argue him in. This week, pray for him by name each morning, asking that the Spirit would convict him about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment. Then, when a door opens, tell him plainly what Christ has done for you. The witness is yours to give. The conviction is the Spirit’s work.

practices.title: TAKE TODAY’S PORTION
practices.body: Jesus held back what His men could not bear. Stop pushing God for the whole map. Each morning, read one short stretch of this passage and write down one thing it says about Christ. Live on that one thing for the day. When the worry asks what happens next month, answer it with what He has already told you. The Spirit gives light for the step you are on.

practices.title: TEST THE VOICE
practices.body: Read John 16:13–15 each morning. Before you name anything as the Spirit’s leading — a job, a move, a hard word to say to someone — ask whether it makes much of Christ and fits His words. Write the passage that supports it beside the decision. The Spirit of truth speaks what He hears. If you cannot find it in what He has already said, do not hang the decision on it.

title: The Spirit of Truth
subtitle: from dust to the Counselor who testifies
keyVerse: However when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.

passage.text: If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you.
If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.
Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.
But they will do all these things to you for my name’s sake, because they don’t know him who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
He who hates me, hates my Father also.
If I hadn’t done among them the works which no one else did, they wouldn’t have had sin. But now they have seen and also hated both me and my Father.
But this happened so that the word may be fulfilled which was written in their law, ‘They hated me without a cause.’
“When the Counselor has come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me.
You will also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.
“I have said these things to you so that you wouldn’t be caused to stumble.
They will put you out of the synagogues. Yes, the time comes that whoever kills you will think that he offers service to God.
They will do these things because they have not known the Father, nor me.
But I have told you these things, so that when the time comes, you may remember that I told you about them. I didn’t tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
But because I have told you these things, sorrow has filled your heart.
Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I don’t go away, the Counselor won’t come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
When he has come, he will convict the world about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment;
about sin, because they don’t believe in me;
about righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you won’t see me any more;
about judgment, because the prince of this world has been judged.
“I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t bear them now.

However when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.
He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine, and will declare it to you.
All things that the Father has are mine; therefore I said that he takes of mine and will declare it to you.

stationsIntro: These five words run from the world’s hatred to the Spirit’s voice. Read each verse slowly, answer the question in plain words, and let the Greek press the verse a little deeper.
lifeIntro: Christ chose you out of the world, told you ahead of time what it would cost, and sent the Spirit of truth to testify about Him. These practices do not earn His presence. They are how a man lives once he knows he has not been left alone.
lifePulls: The Spirit of truth was not sent to make you feel spiritual. He was sent to testify about Christ, to convict the world, and to guide you into the truth by declaring what belongs to the Son.
prayer: Father, You chose me out of the world and gave me to Your Son. Thank You that the world hated Jesus before it hated me, and that He went ahead of me through all of it. When I am mocked or shut out for His name, help me remember what He told me. Take away the excuses I hide behind, and let me bring my sin straight to Christ. Thank You for sending the Counselor, the Spirit of truth, to testify about Jesus. Let Him convict the men I love, and give me plain words to tell them what You have done. Guide us into the truth You have given, and keep us from calling our own wants Your voice. Make much of Christ in me this week. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, You chose me out of the world and gave me to Your Son.
Thank You that the world hated Jesus before it hated me, and that He went ahead
of me through all of it.
When I am mocked or shut out for His name, help me remember what He told me.
Take away the excuses I hide behind, and let me bring my sin straight to Christ.
Thank You for sending the Counselor, the Spirit of truth, to testify about Jesus.
Let Him convict the men I love, and give me plain words to tell them what You
have done.
Guide us into the truth You have given, and keep us from calling our own wants
Your voice.
Make much of Christ in me this week.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: The world hated Jesus first, and it will hate the men He chose out of it. He told them ahead of time so they would not stumble. Then He said His going was their gain, because He would send the Spirit of truth. The Spirit testifies about Christ, convicts the world, and guides into all truth by declaring what belongs to the Son. You have not been left alone with a book. The Spirit speaks through it.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, and listen to who is speaking. Listen to the One the world hated before it ever knew your name. Listen to the One who chose you out of the world and did not ask whether the world would make room for you. Listen to the One who told you the cost before you paid a cent of it, so that when the door slammed you would remember He had said it would. Listen, because He is still speaking, and He has not left you alone.

The dust told you Jesus is far away and you are on your own. But on the night before the cross He said His leaving was your gain. He went to the Father by way of the nails and a garden tomb, and He was raised, and He went up to His Father and your Father. Then He sent the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father. The Spirit is not a mood. He is a Person, sent by the Father and the Son, and He came to stay.

Look at what the Spirit does. He testifies about Jesus when you cannot find the words. He convicts the world of sin, of righteousness and of judgment, so the weight of your son’s soul does not rest on your arguments. He guided the apostles into all truth, and they wrote it down, and He opens that same Word to you now. He does not speak from Himself. He takes what is Christ’s — the cross, the blood, the open grave, the Father’s welcome — and declares it to you.

So carry this into Tuesday, when the mockery comes and your own heart runs dry. You are not alone with a book and your grit. The prince of this world has been judged. The Son has gone to the Father. The Spirit of truth has come, and He will guide you into all truth, and He will glorify Christ to you. Take the word He gives you today. It is enough for today, because it is Christ’s.
closingVerse: However when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak from himself; but whatever he hears, he will speak. He will declare to you things that are coming.
carry: If the Spirit of truth was sent to guide you into all truth by declaring what belongs to Christ, which of the dust’s lies about being left alone will you set against His word this week?

sections.heading: Where the Dust Lies to You
paras: The dust has its own way of telling time. It tells you the hard season you are in is the only season there is. The layoff, the bad scan, the son who will not call — whatever it is, the dust says this is how things are now and how they will stay. Trouble is not one chapter. It is the whole book, and you are near the end of it.

And the dust has a verdict to go with its clock. If trouble keeps coming, the world must be winning. The men who mock Christ seem to do fine. The man who follows Him is short on the fuel bill again. You start to think the people laughing read it right, and that your faith is a way of whistling past a grave.

Some weeks you do not argue with any of that. You just lie down under it. You go to work, you come home, you sit in the truck in the driveway longer than you need to, and the old words come up out of the floor: My soul clings to the dust; Revive me according to Your word. (NKJV)

The word that revives a man there is the last thing Jesus said to His disciples before He lifted up His eyes to pray. He did not tell them trouble was over. He told them it was certain. Then He told them who had already won: I have overcome the world.

sections.heading: The Last Words Before the Prayer
pulls: The dust says the trouble is the whole story. Jesus says the trouble is certain, the sorrow is short, the joy is coming, and the world that troubles you has already been overcome.
paras: This passage closes the long talk Jesus began at the supper table. He has washed their feet, sent Judas into the night, and spent hours telling them what His leaving will mean. Now He says something they cannot make sense of: A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me. They whisper to each other. We don’t know what he is saying.

Jesus answers with a woman in labor, a joy no one can take, and an open door to the Father. Then the disciples say they finally understand, and He tells them that within hours they will scatter and leave Him alone. Notice that He tells them all of it — the grief, the scattering, the trouble — before any of it happens. The last sentence of the passage is the last word before the prayer of John 17. Read 16:16–33 through in one sitting, and listen for the turn from sorrow to joy.

parts.label: PART ONE
parts.heading: A LITTLE WHILE
paras: A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me. Two little whiles. The first ran out within a day, when they took His body down from the cross and laid it in a new tomb in a garden. The second ran out on the first day of the week, when He stood among them behind locked doors and showed them His hands and His side. John tells you what happened then: The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.

But on this night they did not understand. They turned it over among themselves like men trying to read a map in the dark: What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We don’t know what he is saying. There is comfort in that. The men who would carry the gospel to the nations started out confused. Jesus did not scold them. Jesus perceived that they wanted to ask him, and He answered before they asked.

Look at how He measures the time. From where they sat, the days ahead would feel endless. The day of the cross would feel like the end of everything. The Sabbath that followed, with Him in the tomb, would feel like forever. Jesus calls it a little while. He is not making light of their grief. He is telling them it has an edge, a place where it stops, and that He has already set that place.

The man in a hard season needs to hear that. Your trouble is real, and it is also measured. The One who measures it walked out of the grave. He does not ask you to pretend the night is short. He tells you who holds the morning.

parts.label: PART TWO
parts.heading: SORROW TURNED TO JOY
paras: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. Jesus does not hide the order of things. For a while the world would be glad and His friends would grieve. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy. Mark the word turned. He does not say the sorrow will be swapped out for something else, as if He meant to change the subject. The world’s gladness would be short. Theirs would have no end. The very thing that broke them — His death — would become the ground of their joy.

Then He gives them a picture from the birthing room. A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world. Her pain is not fake, and it is not pointless. It is labor. It has a child on the far side of it, and when the child comes the pain loses its hold on her memory.

Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you. Notice who does the seeing. I will see you again. He would come to them alive, and they would rejoice. The same shape holds for you. You live between His rising and His return, and there is sorrow in the between. But your joy is fastened to a risen Christ, and no one can pry it loose — not the world, not the grave, not the bad report. When He comes again, the last tear goes with the last enemy.

parts.label: PART THREE
parts.heading: THE FATHER HIMSELF LOVES YOU
pulls: Jesus knew His men would scatter that very night, and He still told them the Father loves them and the world is beaten. Your failure did not surprise Him, and it does not cancel His peace.
paras: In that day you will ask me no questions. The confusion would not last. After the resurrection and the gift of the Spirit, what was dark that night would be plain. And something else would change. Most certainly I tell you, whatever you may ask of the Father in my name, he will give it to you. Until then they had brought every need to Jesus standing beside them. Now they would come to the Father in the name of the Son, on the ground of all He had done.

Asking in His name is not a password tacked onto the end of a wish list. It means coming as one who belongs to Him, asking for what fits who He is. And the door stands wide: Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full. Prayer is where the joy He promised gets filled to the brim.

Then comes one of the warmest lines in the Gospel. I don’t say to you that I will pray to the Father for you, Jesus says. He does not mean He will never pray for them; in the next chapter He prays for them out loud. He means you need not picture the Father as a hard man who must be talked into kindness. For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came from God. Their love did not buy the Father’s love. It was the sign of it. The Father had drawn them to the Son, and the Father who drew them loves them. You do not come to a grudging God through a willing Christ. You come to a Father who loves you, through the Son He sent.

parts.label: PART FOUR
parts.heading: TROUBLE, AND PEACE IN HIM
paras: Jesus sums up His whole errand in one line: I came from the Father, and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world, and go to the Father. The disciples grab hold of it. Now we know that you know all things, they say. By this we believe that you came from God. It is true faith, and it is thin faith. Jesus answers with a question: Do you now believe?

Then He tells them what the night will bring. Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. He knew. Peter’s boast, Thomas’s questions, Philip’s request — He knew every one of them would scatter. He said it to their faces, and He did not take back one promise He had made that night. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

Then the last word: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up — I have overcome the world. Two places. In the world, trouble, certain and not maybe. In Him, peace. He does not give peace by lifting you out of the world. He gives it by putting you in Him while you are still in it.

And mark the tense. He says it before the arrest, before the whip, before the cross. I have overcome. The victory was as good as done, because the Son had come to finish it, and on the cross He would say so. The world will still trouble you this week. It cannot undo what He has done. The disciples would fail that night. He would not.

stations.verse: A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me.
stations.question: Jesus told confused men that His absence would last a little while and end in seeing Him again, and the empty tomb proved Him right; what present wait on Christ am I treating as if it had no end?
stations.gloss: small, little; as an adverb of time, a little while
body: Mikros means small or little. It is used of short men and of little ones who believe, of the mustard seed and of a little yeast. Used of time it means a short while. Forty-three New Testament verses carry it, and four of them run back to back in 16:16–19.

The disciples got stuck on it. What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? He had told them earlier that night, Yet a little while, and the world will see me no more; but you will see me. Still they could not see past the first little while to the second.

The dust takes your hard season and stretches it into forever. It tells you that what you cannot see now you will never see. Jesus calls the gap a little while, and Hebrews says the same of His return: In a very little while, he who comes will come, and will not wait. The grave He walked out of sets the length of your wait.
stations.live: Name the season where Christ feels out of sight. Each morning this week read John 16:16 aloud, then add: ‘This is a little while. He has set its end, and I will see Him.’

stations.verse: Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.
stations.question: Jesus did not promise His men they would skip the weeping; He promised your sorrow will be turned into joy; what grief of mine am I burying instead of bringing it to the One who said He would turn it?
stations.gloss: to lament, wail; to bewail
body: Thrēneō means to lament, to wail aloud, and with an object, to bewail someone. It is grief that makes a sound. It appears in only four New Testament verses. One of them is on the way to the cross, where women followed Jesus and mourned and lamented him.

Jesus tells His men they will do the same. You will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. He does not tell them grief is a failure of faith. He tells them it is coming, and that it will not have the last word: your sorrow will be turned into joy. They grieved behind locked doors until He came and stood among them.

The dust says a believing man should keep a dry face and a set jaw, or else that his grief proves God has failed him. Jesus allows the lament and then turns it. He does not stand outside your sorrow giving orders. He went into the grave that caused it, and came out to turn it into joy.
stations.live: Bring one grief to God this week without tidying it up. Say it out loud, plainly. Then say: ‘You told me I would lament. You also told me my sorrow will be turned into joy.’

stations.verse: A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world.
stations.question: Jesus compared His men’s grief to a woman’s labor, which ends in a joy that makes her forget the anguish; how does Christ’s rising change the way I carry the sorrow I am in right now?
stations.gloss: to bring forth; to give birth
body: Tiktō properly means to beget or bring forth, and in the New Testament it always means giving birth. The word turns up in 17 verses. Luke uses it of Mary: She gave birth to her firstborn son.

A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. The pain is real, and it has a set hour. But it is pain going somewhere. When the child comes, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more. Their grief at His death would end in the joy of His rising.

The dust tells you your sorrow is a dead end. In Christ, the sorrow of His people is labor. He went into death and came out alive, and the joy born that morning cannot be undone. Your grief does not get the last word, because His grave is empty.
stations.live: Name one sorrow you have filed under pointless. Lay it before Christ each day this week and say: ‘This is labor, not the end. Joy is on the far side, because He is risen.’

stations.verse: Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
stations.question: Jesus told His men they would scatter and leave Him alone, then offered them peace in the next breath; what failure of mine do I think caught Him off guard and cancelled His peace toward me?
stations.gloss: to scatter
body: Skorpizō means to scatter. It occurs in five New Testament verses, two of them in John. In chapter 10 The wolf snatches the sheep, and scatters them. Here the sheep are scattered everyone to his own place, and the Shepherd is left alone.

Jesus said it to their faces, moments after they had told Him, By this we believe that you came from God. He did not call their faith fake. He knew it was not yet strong enough to stand that night. And He did not take back a single promise. The next breath is peace: that in me you may have peace.

The dust says that when you ran, you ran out of His care. But the Shepherd who saw the scattering coming went to the cross for the scattered. When the soldiers came, He said, let these go their way, and John says it fulfilled His word: Of those whom you have given me, I have lost none. He gathers what scatters.
stations.live: Name the time you scattered — the day you went quiet about Christ when it cost something. Bring it to Him plainly, and say: ‘He saw it coming, and He still said peace.’

stations.verse: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.
stations.question: Jesus told men about to see Him crucified, In the world you have trouble; but cheer up, because He had already overcome; where am I waiting for easier days to take heart instead of resting on His victory?
stations.gloss: to be of good courage; take heart
body: Tharseō means to be of good courage. In all seven New Testament verses where it appears, it comes as a command, and six times from the Lord Himself. He said it to a paralyzed man, Son, cheer up, and forgave his sins. He said it to frightened men on the water, and to Paul in the barracks.

Here it closes the upper room. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up. Jesus does not ground the command in better weather. He grounds it in a finished fact: I have overcome the world. The courage He commands is not a mood you work up. It is the fitting answer to what He has done.

The dust says take heart when things improve. Jesus says take heart now, in the trouble, because the outcome is settled. The paralyzed man heard that word before he ever stood up. Your courage this week does not rest on how the week goes. It rests on who won.
stations.live: Write John 16:33 on a card and keep it in your shirt pocket or lunch pail. When trouble comes this week, read it once, slowly, and say: ‘He told me it would come. He has overcome.’

practices.title: LET HIM SET THE LENGTH
practices.body: Name the hardest thing you are waiting on — the job, the diagnosis, the son who left. Read John 16:16–22 at the start of each day. Each time, say the length Jesus gave His men: a little while. You are not pretending the wait is short. You are letting Him set its length instead of your fear. Then do the day’s work in front of you. A man who believes the wait has an end can still mend a fence on Wednesday.

practices.title: LAMENT TO GOD, NOT AROUND HIM
practices.body: Jesus told His men they would weep and lament. He did not shame them for it. This week, take the grief you have been carrying quietly and say it to God in plain words — in the cab, on the porch, on a walk along the back field. Do not dress it up. Then read 16:20–22 and thank Him that your sorrow is tied to His resurrection. Lament that goes to God is not unbelief. It is a man taking his grief to the One who will turn it.

practices.title: ASK THE FATHER
practices.body: Jesus said the Father himself loves you. Pray this week as a son to that Father, in the name of Christ. Bring Him the specific things: the bill, the son, the temptation you keep losing to. Do not pile on words. Ask, and trust Him to answer in the way that fills your joy, not your wish list. Close each prayer by thanking Him that you come on Christ’s ground, not your own.

practices.title: OWN YOUR SCATTERING
practices.body: Think of a recent time you went quiet about Christ or backed away when it cost something. Do not bury it, and do not wallow in it. Tell God plainly. Then read John 16:32–33 together. He knew His men would scatter, and in the next breath He gave them peace. If your silence left someone without a word they needed — a man at work, your wife, your boy — go back this week and say it.

practices.title: TAKE HEART ON PURPOSE
practices.body: Put John 16:33 where you will see it every day — the dash, the tool bench, the bathroom mirror. When the news, the bank or the doctor brings trouble this week, read it aloud. Then name one thing Christ has already overcome for you: the guilt of your sin, the claim of death, the accuser’s case. Courage in this verse is a command Jesus gives because the fight is already won. Obey it before you feel it.

title: I Have Overcome the World
subtitle: from dust to peace in Him
keyVerse: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.

passage.text: A little while, and you will not see me. Again a little while, and you will see me.”

Some of his disciples therefore said to one another, “What is this that he says to us, ‘A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me;’ and, ‘Because I go to the Father’?”
They said therefore, “What is this that he says, ‘A little while’? We don’t know what he is saying.”

Therefore Jesus perceived that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, “Do you inquire among yourselves concerning this, that I said, ‘A little while, and you won’t see me, and again a little while, and you will see me?’
Most certainly I tell you that you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow because her time has come. But when she has delivered the child, she doesn’t remember the anguish any more, for the joy that a human being is born into the world.
Therefore you now have sorrow, but I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
“In that day you will ask me no questions. Most certainly I tell you, whatever you may ask of the Father in my name, he will give it to you.
Until now, you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be made full.
I have spoken these things to you in figures of speech. But the time is coming when I will no more speak to you in figures of speech, but will tell you plainly about the Father.
In that day you will ask in my name; and I don’t say to you that I will pray to the Father for you,
for the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me, and have believed that I came from God.
I came from the Father, and have come into the world. Again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.”
His disciples said to him, “Behold, now you are speaking plainly, and using no figures of speech.
Now we know that you know all things, and don’t need for anyone to question you. By this we believe that you came from God.”
Jesus answered them, “Do you now believe?
Behold, the time is coming, yes, and has now come, that you will be scattered, everyone to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.”

stationsIntro: These five words run from a little while of grief to the last command spoken in the upper room. Read each verse, answer the question plainly, and let the Greek bring you back to the One who has overcome.
lifeIntro: Jesus went to the cross knowing His friends would scatter, and He still promised them peace, a joy no one could take, and a Father who loves them. He has overcome the world. These practices are what a man does when he believes that in a week that still has trouble in it.
lifePulls: Trouble in the world is certain. Peace in Christ is just as certain. But the trouble is passing, and the One who gives the peace has already overcome the world.
prayer: Father, Your Son told us the truth: in the world we have trouble. Thank You that He also told us He has overcome the world. When I cannot see Him, remind me that the wait is a little while. Turn my sorrow into joy, the way You turned the grief of His friends when He stood among them alive. Thank You that You Yourself love me, and that I may ask in Jesus’ name. Forgive me for the times I have scattered and left Him alone. Thank You that He saw it coming and still gave me peace. Keep my brothers in Christ when they scatter, and gather us again to You. Give me courage this week that rests on His victory and not on my circumstances. In Jesus’ name, amen.
prayerLines: Father, Your Son told us the truth: in the world we have trouble.
Thank You that He also told us He has overcome the world.
When I cannot see Him, remind me that the wait is a little while.
Turn my sorrow into joy, the way You turned the grief of His friends when He
stood among them alive.
Thank You that You Yourself love me, and that I may ask in Jesus’ name.
Forgive me for the times I have scattered and left Him alone.
Thank You that He saw it coming and still gave me peace.
Keep my brothers in Christ when they scatter, and gather us again to You.
Give me courage this week that rests on His victory and not on my
circumstances.
In Jesus’ name, amen.
bottomLine: Jesus told His men they would lose sight of Him for a little while and then see Him again. Their sorrow would be like labor, turned into a joy no one could take. The Father Himself loves them, and they could ask in the Son’s name. They would scatter that night, and He told them so. Then He gave them His last word: trouble in the world, peace in Him, and the world already overcome.
benediction: Lift up your eyes, dusty soul, and look back down the road John has walked you through. See the tomb at Bethany, and hear the loud voice: Lazarus, come out. See the house filled with the fragrance of the ointment Mary poured on His feet. See the grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies, and the Son lifted up from the earth to draw men to Himself. See the towel around His waist and the basin in His hands, and hear the new commandment: Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.

Hear Him promise the Father’s house with its many homes, and another Counselor who stays with you forever. See the true Vine, and yourself a branch in it. Hear Him send the Spirit of truth to take what is His and declare it to you. Then come into this last stretch of the upper room, where He tells frightened men about a little while, a woman in labor, and a joy no one will take. It is one Christ through all of it, and every gift in these chapters comes from His hand.

Then hear the hardest thing. He told them they would scatter, and they did. He knew it of you too, before you ever ran. And He did not answer with a threat. He answered with peace: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. Next John will take you into the prayer He prayed for His own, to the cross where He said It is finished, and to the tomb Mary Magdalene found open and empty.

But stand here first, where He stood that night. The world will trouble you this week. The bill will come, the back will ache, and someone will sneer at the name you carry. None of it surprises Him. He named it before you met it, and He has gone through death and out the other side. The cross was where the world was beaten. So take heart, dusty soul. In the world you have trouble, and in Him you have peace, because He has overcome the world.
closingVerse: I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.
carry: Knowing they would scatter that very night, Jesus still told His men in me you may have peace; what trouble in front of you this week will you face as a man whose Lord has already overcome the world?
